newsitem.title: USA: Chase, Chemical post strong fourth-quarter results.
newsitem.headline: Chase, Chemical post strong fourth-quarter results.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp. and Citicorp, the nation's two largest banking companies, Tuesday reported healthy earnings gains in their fourth quarters, continuing the strong year-end trend among major banks.
Wells Fargo and Co., the nation's eighth-ranked bank, reported a drop in profits -- sharply below analysts' expectations -- related to its merger with First Interstate Bancorp.

Chase said it earned $836 million, or $1.74 a share, compared with $827 million, or $1.73 cents a share, a year earlier. The latest results included costs related to its merger with Chemical Banking Corp.
Revenues increased to $3.94 billion from $3.84 billion.
Chase and Chemical merged in March, creating the nation's largest banking company.
Excluding the merger-related costs, Chase earned $901 million, or $1.89 a share, up from $827 million, or $1.73 a share, a year earlier.
While the results were about equal to Wall Street's expectations, Chase's shares were lower in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, off 50 cents at $92.375 after earlier falling $1.25.

Citicorp, the nation's second-largest banking company, said it earned $987 million, or $1.97 a share, on revenue of $5.75 billion, in the fourth quarter. A year earlier, the company earned $905 million, or $1.72 a share, on revenue of $5.05 billion.
Its earnings were slightly better than the $1.95 a share anticipated by Wall Street analysts surveyed by First Call, and its stock gained $2.625 to $111.625 on the NYSE.

Wells Fargo reported fourth-quarter earnings of $123 million, or $1.12 a share, compared with $306 million, or $6.29 a share, in 1995's fourth quarter. Analysts on average had expected the bank to post earnings of $2.86 per share for the quarter, according to First Call.
The company said its latest results were not comparable to the year-ago quarter because of the First Interstate merger.
Wells Fargo stock rose $8.25 to $288 on the NYSE.
Analysts said the results showed business continues to be profitable despite slippage in its U.S. credit card business.

Brown Brothers Harriman brokerage analyst Raphael Soifer said that, for now, loss rates in the credit card business are being covered by credit card profits. He said that with loss rates above 5 percent in a growing economy, the concern is what losses would look like if the economy slips into recession.

Chase said its increase in revenue and its reduction in expenses were greater than its targets for both the quarter and the year. The provision for credit losses was $182 million for the quarter and $897 million for the year, reflecting strong asset quality, it said.
In addition, Chase repurchased $1 billion of its common stock during the quarter.

For the year, Chase earned $2.46 billion, or $5.02 a share, on revenue of $15.86 billion. A year earlier, the company earned $2.96 billion, or $6.20 a share, on revenue of $14.96 billion. Excluding merger-related costs, Chase earned $3.59 billion, up from $2.98 billion, in 1995.
Total assets were $336 billion as of Dec. 31, up from $304 billion a year earlier.
"Led by strong earnings across the full breadth of our businesses, Chase had an excellent year and quarter," said Chairman Walter V. Shipley.
Citicorp said its domestic credit card business was off, but overseas consumer business and corporate business around the world improved.

"It was a very solid quarter. The retail banking business globally is on a tear," said Robert Albertson, an analyst with Goldman, Sachs & Co. "Credit cards are up from last quarter thanks to overseas."
For the year, Citicorp earned $3.78 billion, or $7.42 a share, on revenue of $21.54 billion. A year earlier, the company earned $3.46 billion, or $6.48 a share, on revenue of $19.62 billion.

"We continued to produce strong financial results with excellent returns," said Chairman John S. Reed. "At the same time, we invested in our growing franchises, in line with our business directions strategy of serving corporate and consumer customers around the world."
Citicorp said it repurchased $820 million worth of its common stock during the quarter.
Its total assets were $281 billion on Dec. 31, up from $257 billion a year earlier.
For the year, Wells Fargo earned $1.071 billion, or $12.21 a share, vs. $1.032 billion, or $20.37 per share. Its total assets were $107.3 million, down from $109.2 million a year earlier.
